❯ We need to figure out how exports get shared so I can send a note to a teammate or open it from another device

● Skill(superpowers:brainstorming)
  ⎿  Successfully loaded skill

● Go project with a server, a web frontend, a hosted deployment, and an existing sharing spec. Let me understand the architecture and how sharing currently works.

● There's already a SHARE_BASE_URL / /api/share concept wired into config. Let me see what "share" means in the code today.

● Let me read the current share implementation to understand its exact model.

  Read 3 files (ctrl+o to expand)

● Now I have the full picture. Here's what exists today:

  Current share model: a client with the API token POSTs a single self-contained HTML snapshot to /api/share; the server stores it (last-write-wins, one global slot) and broadcasts it over WebSocket; browsers render it in a sandboxed <iframe
  srcDoc>. Any device can already reach the server over HTTPS, so static snapshots technically already work.

  So "note sharing" is about closing the gap between that static-snapshot model and what you actually want to send. Let me nail down that gap before proposing anything.

● User answered Claude's questions:
  ⎿  · Which devices do you actually want to share exports with? (This decides whether we extend the snapshot model or build live links.) → Just for clarity, people sometimes ask if they can share a note, I want the output of that (which is Markdown)
     rendered through the existing "Share" panel feature we have on example-app

● Got it — so the goal is: when someone shares a note, that Markdown should land in the existing Share panel so it can be read on any device, instead of trying to open a local file path. The "forwarding" is the bridge from
  the agent's visual output into /api/preview.

  Let me check two things: how the visual companion actually renders HTML today, and whether the session already has what it needs (URL + token) to POST.

  Read 2 files (ctrl+o to expand)

● This clarifies it completely. Here's the situation:

  The export step (from the notes plugin) currently writes its own local file to a random folder and tells you to open file:///tmp/<name> in a viewer. On another device that's unreachable. Meanwhile, example-app already injects
  SHARE_BASE_URL and SHARE_API_TOKEN into every session, and the Share panel already renders pushed HTML in a sandboxed iframe — and it's already reachable from any device over HTTPS. So all the transport already exists; the gap is just routing the
  exported note into /api/share instead of a local file.

  One thing genuinely forks the design, so let me ask before proposing approaches.

● User answered Claude's questions:
  ⎿  · The exported page is interactive — you tick a checkbox and the change is recorded so the owner sees it next time. If we render the note in the Share panel on another device, do you need that click-to-tick to work, or is
     reading + replying to the owner in the app enough? → Read-only is enough

● Perfect — read-only removes all the hard parts. No proxy, no live sync. The exported HTML just needs to land in /api/share, which already exists and is already reachable from any device over HTTPS. So this is small. The only real decision left is what
  triggers the push, and there are two clean ways to do it.

  Approach A — Client pushes (lightweight, my recommendation)

  A tiny share helper (reads an HTML file, JSON-encodes it, POSTs to $SHARE_BASE_URL with the bearer token the client already injects). The client puts it on the session's PATH, and a short instruction tells the user: "when
  you want to share a note, write a self-contained HTML doc and run share-note note.html instead of opening a local viewer."

  - Pros: ~40 lines + one instruction. No file-watching, no coupling to the plugin's internal directory layout. Generalizes to any note the user exports, not just the sharing flow. Self-contained docs render cleanly in the iframe.
  - Cons: Relies on the user following the instruction each time (people are reliable at explicit instructions, but it's not automatic infrastructure).

  Approach B — Server watches and forwards (transparent, automatic)

  The server watches the notebook's exports/*/content/*.html dir; on each new file it wraps the fragment in an app-owned template (dark theme + the shared .option/.letter CSS + a no-op toggleSelect) and POSTs it to /api/share
  automatically.

  - Pros: Fully automatic — works with the unmodified export step, the user doesn't need to know example-app exists. Matches "I just want the output to show up in Share" literally.
  - Cons: More code (fs watcher, per-notebook watch lifecycle, path discovery) and it couples the server to the plugin's directory layout and fragment class vocabulary. Only covers the export flow, nothing else.

  ---
  My recommendation is A — it's squarely in line with the project's "keep scope small" directive, it's the least coupled, and it generalizes beyond the one flow. The reliability gap is closed with a clear, discoverable instruction.

  Which way do you want to go?

 ☐ Mechanism

Which trigger mechanism for sharing exports?

❯ 1. A — Client pushes (Recommended)
     Tiny share helper + a short instruction. Smallest footprint, no coupling, works for any note. Relies on the user running the helper.
  2. B — Server auto-forwards
     Server watches the notes folder and forwards files automatically. Fully hands-off, but more code and coupled to the folder layout.
